Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences, recent intent, and multiple latent interests. MISER (2024) combines temporal analysis with multi-interest contrastive learning; a 2025 hierarchical model uses dynamic routing for long-term interest vectors, self-attention for recent interactions, and time encoding to fuse the relevant interests. These offer architectural ideas without requiring ownership or purchase-intent labels. [MISER](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705124012917), [hierarchical model](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y).

Efficiency-oriented directions include RecGRELA (2025, revised 2026), combining linear attention, local token mixing, and gates balancing transient versus stable preferences. TME-PSR (2026 preprint) introduces gated temporal encoding and lightweight multihead linear recurrent units for separate sub-interests. A practical adaptation to test: retain SASRec’s recent-context encoder, add a small bank of attention-pooled historical interests, and learn fusion gates from observed time gaps, history length, and recent/history similarity. This is an implementation hypothesis, not an established improvement on the four-category benchmark. [RecGRELA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13315), [TME-PSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09439).

Replenishment evidence needs caution: MgRIA (2026) models repeated-purchase timing through multiple periodicities and interval-aware scoring. Its setting differs from unseen-item recommendation, where direct item repurchase cannot help. Transferable idea: learn temporal decay or recurrence of latent interests, allowing category-specific behavior. Interaction histories alone do not establish ownership, satisfied needs, or durable-goods replacement cycles; any recency suppression should be learned and validated rather than imposed. [MgRIA](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037).

---

Evidence supports testing the training objective before changing SASRec’s architecture. [Turning Dross Into Gold Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) reports that full-softmax cross-entropy substantially improves SASRec, and sampled training remains competitive when using many more than one negative. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) combines additional negatives with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence. These support separate multi-negative softmax and gBCE baselines; neither establishes improvement on this RecHarness benchmark.

Recent hard-negative methods offer useful mechanisms, but distinguish sequence-level contrastive learning from next-item candidate ranking. [NARec (2025)](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/aie2.70004) selects hard negatives from batch/global pools and learns negative augmentations. [FENRec (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/33287/35442) mixes anchors with negatives after warm-up to sustain contrastive difficulty, alongside time-dependent soft labels. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses suspected false negatives through teacher soft labels and consistency regularization. High similarity therefore signals both informativeness and possible false-negative risk.

Practical inference for the GPU budget: first compare single-negative BCE against candidate softmax with 32–128 uniform negatives and multi-negative gBCE. Then test a small hard-negative fraction mined from a bounded random pool after warm-up, retaining uniform negatives. Exclude padding, target collisions and known training-history positives; deduplicate candidates. Treat these settings as proposed ablations, not published optima. Nonuniform sampling requires explicit consideration of sampling correction when approximating full softmax. Select exclusively by four-category macro validation HR@10; weaker Electronics training margins alone do not justify increased hardness.

---

Recent work supports separating item similarity from complementarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734) models complements through both relevance and dissimilarity, combining low-pass and mid-pass graph filters with attention. This suggests that smoothing all connected items toward similar embeddings can lose useful complementary structure. [DAKSR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.is.2024.102470) explicitly incorporates item–item knowledge-graph correlations into sequential recommendation, but its external relation information is unavailable here. Neither approach establishes that consecutive interactions alone identify complements or product compatibility.

The no-pretrained-weights constraint excludes prominent text-based approaches such as [WhitenRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602), which operates on pretrained text embeddings. An older relevant precedent, [Sceptre](https://cs.stanford.edu/people/jure/pubs/prodgraph-kdd15.pdf), learns substitute/complement relationships using product text and topic models, though its original inputs and relation supervision exceed this task’s available evidence. A feasible experimental adaptation—not a verified result from these papers—is to retain SASRec, learn a small token-embedding encoder from available titles/descriptions, and add separately weighted text-match and directed transition scores. Train all parameters from scratch using training histories; preserve item-ID residuals to distinguish near-identical titles. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting features score candidate items through shared item embeddings. Training uses shifted next-item targets and sampled negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
